predictions.hypothesis: A second native Ethernet initialization after initial startup is useful, beyond simply waiting for the same final release edge.
predictions.test: F401 enabled vs hold have the same final digital release edge; only enabled has a reset-free gap and a second pulse.
predictions.prediction: Enabled reliable, hold and bypass unreliable.

predictions.hypothesis: A longer initial public reset or a later final release is sufficient.
predictions.test: F401 hold without any second attempt.
predictions.prediction: Hold improves similarly to enabled; does not establish a unique physical settling mechanism.

predictions.hypothesis: Starting native GT sequencing at SYS lock instead of after the original2.147s global POR avoids the problematic startup history.
predictions.test: F402 same-route early control forwards raw SYS-lock reset only. If promising, separately compile and test a one-line source candidate.
predictions.prediction: Raw-only can work with no new production timer. Diagnostic control alone is not proof of a one-line source build.

predictions.hypothesis: One extra unconditional reset is insufficient under some initial states.
predictions.test: Expand enabled cold trials, long OFF and read-only traffic soak on both boards.
predictions.prediction: Any enabled failure weakens the minimum one-shot proposal and must be retained; do not adopt based only on initial3/3.

clock_dependency_fact: Source and freshDCP show independentSYS timer clock125MHz, GTindependentclock200MHz, CPLL selected00, common POR reachesunusedQPLLreset. Publicreset restarts native PCS/TX/RX sequencing; RXPMARESET pin itself remains0.
limits: No dedicated MGT rail, reference jitter or physical SFP input-start waveform measurement in this minimum image.
Input-stream/refclock startup ordering is a hypothesis, not an observed initiating cause.
Equal release means equal RTL/SYS-cycle edge and common gate route within the matched design; analog phases across different power cycles are not controlled.
Prior RX recovered-clock anomaly is separate measured evidence; a new network success does not itself measure CDR lock or frequency.
